pr_title: Bluetooth: controller: fix post DLE/PHY update event length
pr_body:
Fix the controller implementation to perform connection event length reservation based on the completed Data Length Update and/or PHY Update Procedure.

Note: some optimisation is possible with regards to the length allocated, currently the maximum rx and tx time are used, which leaves a lot of unused airtime in case that the 2M phy is used. If necessary this will be fixed in a separate PR
fixes #21995
fixes #52393
Fixes #53049

Signed-off-by: Andries Kruithof <andries.kruithof@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: A thought - couldn't we know (ie remember) the sum of current ready_delay and tx/rx time contributions, so that we only need to calc the difference (to get the slot_plus/minus) to perform the ticker update? Instead of doing the 'full monty'?

> A thought - couldn't we know (ie remember) the sum of current ready_delay and tx/rx time contributions, so that we only need to calc the difference (to get the slot_plus/minus) to perform the ticker update? Instead of doing the 'full monty'?

We could, but it is a trade-off between memory usage and processor time. These calculations are only done occasionally, so no big effect on processing time

issue_context.title: Controller: ACL packets NACKed after Data Length Update
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When central is connected to multiple peripherals and the ~MTU~ LL data length is increased to 247 bytes, central gets notifications only from the last connected peripheral

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Central connects to more than one peripheral
2. For each connection, set the connection interval to be 25 ms
3. For each connection, increase the MTU above 190 bytes
4. Send notifications from connected peripherals other than the last connected one

**Expected behavior**
1. Central receives notifications from the last connected peripheral
2. Notifications from peripherals other than the last connected one are missed
3. Peripherals that aren't communicating disconnect with time out disconnection reason

**Additional context**
Issue doesn't occur if the connection interval is increased or the notification data size is below 160 bytes

**Environment**
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
 - Toolchain : Zephyr SDK 0.15.1
 - Commit SHA 3607a05fbaf1d85a1e11d19c6ff33b869c5e88bb
 - PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/52392
comments:
I think it's a controller issue, the test works fine (there were some logic errors) when peripherals are compiled with `CONFIG_BT_AUTO_DATA_LEN_UPDATE=n`.

It seems the central controller has issues ACK-ing one of the peripheral after switching to the max LL packet length. When the LL data length stays at 27, there are no issues whatsoever. 

@kruithofa and @cvinayak To reproduce:
- check out this branch: https://github.com/jori-nordic/zephyr/tree/long-packets-no-ack
- run the build&test script `tests/bluetooth/bsim_bt/bsim_test_conn_stress/tests_scripts/conn_stress.sh`

I've tested the same scenario using the desktop application "nrf connect for desktop Bluetooth Low Energy" in place of the central device while keeping the same peripherals and following the same behavior of the central application and there were no issues found.

So, I support @jori-nordic assumption that the central controller has an issue
might be fixed by PR #52012 and #53095, I will reproduce the issue first, and see if these PRs fix it

review_comments:
In my perspective, updating the slot reservation based on DLE `max_octets` is incorrect for this controller. The ticker shall only reserve the time needed for basic LL transactions, i.e. for a PDU size of 27 bytes in each direction.
Using `max_octets` will cause too heavy reservations for ACL connections, causing substantial scheduling collisions.

So this PR will significantly change the behaviour of the controller. For some users it will improve, but for others it may cause issues.
Proposal: add a KConfig (marked experimental) for modifying the slotreservation, default set to off, so that behaviour is unchanged per default, but users seeing issues can enable this new slotreservation. Only allow setting it to on when the maximum nr. of connections is 2 or higher
